correctness.rationale: Proposition 6.3 uses ε/2 in the tensor and b=exp(−2C/ε). Writing a=p(1−p), the off-diagonal self-coupling w solves B w²+w=a. Substitution yields g=εB/(2√(1+4Ba)), including a finite positive boundary extension. The coordinate obtained by integrating √g is an isometry to an interval with Euclidean distance, proving the constant-speed inverse and its normalization. On the left half interval, the normalized density ratio for β₁<β₂ strictly decreases and both densities have half their mass there, implying strict CDF order; comparison to the uniform density and reflection give the full inequalities. L¹ convergence of the densities gives uniform CDF convergence and uniform convergence of the inverses to the beta quantile. After u=βv the left-end loss, divided by β^(3/4), is dominated by a constant times min(v^(−1/4),v^(−5/4)) on a fixed short endpoint neighborhood. Its integral limit is 4/3 by explicit antidifferentiation. The right-end loss is identical and the rest is O(β), uniformly for fixed compact interior ranges of the upper limit. The inverse equation therefore gives the claimed interior coefficient, including zero at the midpoint. The rescaled arclength from zero to βy converges locally uniformly to (4/3)((1+y)^(3/4)−1), which is strictly increasing and unbounded; inversion proves the endpoint profile including s=0. Zβ→K and the exact prefactor prove the distance equivalent.
